issue.title: [Moonshot] Reject unsupported required tool choice by model
issue.body:
## Endpoint and priority

`POST /v1/chat/completions` — **P0** because unsupported `tool_choice: "required"` requests are currently sent unchanged.

## Official specification evidence

The [model-parameter guide](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/models-overview) documents required tool choice for K3 and says K2.6/K2.7 return an error. The [OpenAPI document](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) defines the common wire value.

## Current behavior

`prepareTools` forwards `required` for every model.

## Expected behavior

Keep `required` for documented supporting models and custom IDs, but omit it with an actionable warning for explicitly unsupported models.

## Proposed implementation

Pass model capability into tool preparation or gate its result in request preparation.

## Acceptance criteria

- K3 sends `required`.
- K2.6/K2.7 omit it and warn.
- Other tool-choice modes remain unchanged.
- Unknown IDs remain compatible.

## Required artifacts

Unit tests for request bodies/warnings and tool preparation; no fixture/type/docs example required unless public types change; documentation note; patch changeset.

## Backport applicability

Expected applicable to v6 and v5 if their warning contracts can represent omission; adapt warning shapes per release.

issue.title: [Moonshot] Accept documented streaming chunk variants
issue.body:
## Endpoint and priority

`POST /v1/chat/completions` SSE response — **P0** because the current validation can reject an officially conforming chunk and can lose documented usage.

## Official specification evidence

The [OpenAPI `ChoiceDelta` schema](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) omits tool-call `index` and includes optional choice-level `usage`; `ChatCompletionChunk` also defines top-level usage. First-party examples commonly include tool-call indices and top-level final usage, so both variants must be tolerated.

## Current behavior

Streaming tool-call `index` is required by the parser, while choice-level usage is ignored.

## Expected behavior

Accept tool calls with or without an explicit index and collect usage from either documented location, preferring the top-level value when both occur.

## Proposed implementation

Make index nullish in the wire schema, derive a deterministic per-array fallback index for the tracker, add choice usage to the schema, and normalize usage selection.

## Acceptance criteria

- Index-less tool-call chunks parse and assemble correctly.
- Explicit indices retain current behavior.
- Top-level and choice-level usage variants produce correct totals.
- Malformed chunks still surface validation errors.

## Required artifacts

Captured-style SSE fixtures and streaming unit tests; no public type/docs/example required; patch changeset.

## Backport applicability

- v6: expected applicable because it owns stream parsing.
- v5: only applicable if the generic OpenAI-compatible stream parser has the same rejection/loss and a provider-local fix is possible; otherwise document as not applicable.

issue.title: `@ai-sdk/mcp` does not apply MCP scope selection during Dynamic Client Registration
issue.body:
### Description

Follow-up to #18813 / #18818.

`#18818` applies the MCP scope-selection strategy when building the **authorization URL**. Dynamic Client Registration still ignores those same scopes.

`authInternal` has already fetched Protected Resource Metadata (including `scopes_supported`) before it calls `registerClient`, but it passes `provider.clientMetadata` through unchanged. If the app did not set `clientMetadata.scope`, the RFC 7591 register body omits `scope`.

Some authorization servers then register the client with a default scope set that is **not** the resource’s `scopes_supported`. Later authorize requests that do include the PRM scopes can still be limited to that DCR default.

This is the same gap n8n fixed in https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/32300: copy `scopes_supported` from RFC 9728 PRM into **both** DCR and the authorization request, preferring PRM over authorization-server metadata (which often omits `scopes_supported`).

Relevant specs:

- [MCP Scope Selection Strategy](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization#scope-selection-strategy)
- [RFC 7591 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591.html#section-2) (`scope` in client metadata = scopes the client may request)
- [RFC 9728](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9728.html) (`scopes_supported` on the protected resource)

Real-world example: Atlassian Rovo MCP (`https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2`) advertises classic scopes such as `read:jira-work` on [PRM](https://mcp.atlassian.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp/authv2), but its AS metadata has no `scopes_supported`. Registering without `scope` yields a client/token with preview `*:agent-interface` scopes; tool calls on that resource then fail with `401 Unauthorized; scope does not match`.

### Expected behavior

When `provider.clientMetadata.scope` is unset, DCR should use the same `selectScope()` result as authorize:

1. `WWW-Authenticate` `scope`, if present
2. Else PRM `scopes_supported` joined with spaces
3. Else omit `scope`

### Actual behavior

`registerClient` stringifies `provider.clientMetadata` as-is. With no `clientMetadata.scope`, the register body has no `scope`, even though PRM advertised `scopes_supported` and the subsequent authorize URL (after #18818) includes those scopes.

### Reproduction

Start an OAuth flow with no `clientMetadata.scope` and no pre-registered `clientInformation`. Have PRM advertise `scopes_supported`. Inspect the DCR `POST` body: `scope` is missing.

<details>
<summary>Minimal runnable reproduction</summary>

```js
import { auth } from "@ai-sdk/mcp"

let dcrBody
let authorizationUrl

const provider = {
  redirectUrl: "https://client.example.com/callback",
  clientMetadata: {
    client_name: "Reproduction",
    redirect_uris: ["https://client.example.com/callback"],
    token_endpoint_auth_method: "none",
  },
  clientInformation: () => undefined,
  saveClientInformation: () => {},
  tokens: () => undefined,
  saveTokens: () => {},
  saveCodeVerifier: () => {},
  codeVerifier: () => "unused",
  redirectToAuthorization: (url) => {
    authorizationUrl = url
  },
}

const fetchFn = async (input, init) => {
  const url = new URL(input.toString())

  if (url.pathname.includes("/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource")) {
    return Response.json({
      resource: "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      authorization_servers: ["https://auth.example.com"],
      scopes_supported: ["mcp.read", "mcp.write"],
    })
  }

  if (url.pathname.includes("/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server")) {
    return Response.json({
      issuer: "https://auth.example.com",
      authorization_endpoint: "https://auth.example.com/authorize",
      token_endpoint: "https://auth.example.com/token",
      registration_endpoint: "https://auth.example.com/register",
      response_types_supported: ["code"],
      code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"],
    })
  }

  if (url.pathname === "/register" && init?.method === "POST") {
    dcrBody = JSON.parse(String(init.body))
    return Response.json({
      client_id: "test-client",
      client_id_issued_at: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
    })
  }

  return new Response(null, { status: 404 })
}

await auth(provider, {
  serverUrl: "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
  fetchFn,
})

console.log("dcr scope:", dcrBody?.scope)
console.log("authorize scope:", authorizationUrl.searchParams.get("scope"))
```

</details>

Expected:

```text
dcr scope: mcp.read mcp.write
authorize scope: mcp.read mcp.write
```

Actual (verified against `packages/mcp/src/tool/oauth.ts` on `main`: `registerClient` uses `provider.clientMetadata`; `selectScope` is only passed into `startAuthorization`):

```text
dcr scope: undefined
authorize scope: mcp.read mcp.write
```

### AI SDK Version

`@ai-sdk/mcp@1.0.71` (v6) and current `main` (`@ai-sdk/mcp` 2.x, post-#18818).

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

issue.title: [Moonshot] Gate sampling parameters by model
issue.body:
## Endpoint and priority

`POST /v1/chat/completions` — **P0** because the provider currently emits request fields that documented Kimi models reject.

## Official specification evidence

The [model-parameter guide](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/models-overview) says Kimi K3/K2.7/K2.6/K2.5 use fixed sampling and explicit `temperature`, `top_p`, `presence_penalty`, or `frequency_penalty` modifications cause errors. The [OpenAPI document](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) defines those fields only on `MoonshotV1ChatRequest`, with ranges `0..1` and `-2..2`.

## Current behavior

Generic sampling call options are forwarded for every model.

## Expected behavior

Send supported sampling fields for Moonshot V1. Omit them with actionable warnings for Kimi models. Preserve custom-model compatibility rather than guessing restrictions for unknown IDs.

## Proposed implementation

Add model capability detection in request preparation, omit unsupported fields, and emit one warning per supplied setting.

## Acceptance criteria

- Kimi requests omit all four sampling fields and return warnings.
- Moonshot V1 requests retain valid values.
- Unknown custom model IDs retain current pass-through behavior.
- Existing unaffected requests do not change.

## Required artifacts

Unit tests for Kimi/V1/custom request bodies and warnings; type tests only if public types change; no fixture required; provider documentation note and a focused example if public guidance benefits; patch changeset.

## Backport applicability

- v6: expected applicable; it owns request preparation.
- v5: expected applicable through the OpenAI-compatible settings/body path if it can omit generic settings without provider-interface expansion; otherwise document concrete interface evidence as not applicable.

issue.title: [Moonshot] Validate multimodal MIME types
issue.body:
## Endpoint and priority

`POST /v1/chat/completions` — **P0** because unsupported media is serialized into requests the API rejects.

## Official specification evidence

The [vision guide](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-vision-model) lists supported image MIME types (`jpeg`, `png`, `gif`, `webp`, `bmp`, `heic`, `heif`) and video MIME types (`mp4`, `mpeg`, `mov`, `avi`, `x-flv`, `mpg`, `webm`, `wmv`, `3gpp`), and explicitly rejects SVG/external image URLs.

## Current behavior

The converter accepts every `image/*` and `video/*` media type. External URLs are correctly downloaded/inlined by the core URL support policy, but unsupported encoded MIME types still pass through.

## Expected behavior

Serialize only official MIME types and raise `UnsupportedFunctionalityError` before sending unsupported media.

## Proposed implementation

Add explicit MIME allowlists around image/video conversion while retaining wildcard URL handling and `ms://` support.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every documented MIME type is accepted.
- Representative unsupported types, including SVG, are rejected locally.
- Data URI and URL/reference behavior remains correct.

## Required artifacts

Converter and language-model unit tests; no type tests/fixtures/docs example required beyond a supported-format documentation note; patch changeset.

## Backport applicability

- v6: expected applicable because it owns multimodal conversion.
- v5: likely not applicable because that release uses the generic OpenAI-compatible converter and lacks Moonshot video conversion; confirm with concrete release code.

issue.title: Turbopack: mangle exports behind an escaping namespace via the facade
issue.body:
### What?

Stacked on #97676. Turbopack backs off from export mangling entirely when a module's
namespace object escapes — an `import * as ns` whose reads can't be enumerated, or a
dynamic `import()` — so one such import un-mangles the whole module. Webpack does
better: it keeps mangling the internal keys and *materializes* a namespace object that
maps the original names onto them. This makes Turbopack do the same, using the facade /
locals split it already has.

It also fixes a latent bug in that machinery (see the third bullet below) and unblocks a
tree-shaking case Turbopack previously couldn't handle.

### Why?

`import * as ns` is common — a single one in a dependency currently costs mangling for
every export of that module. This was the largest remaining gap noted as a follow-up on
#97672.

### How?

**The facade could not tell the locals module what it needed.**
`EcmascriptModuleFacadeModule::references()` exposed exactly one edge to the locals
module, hard-coded `ExportUsage::all()`. That wasn't a conservative choice about
namespaces — the facade's *real* per-export references are synthesized in
`get_exports()` for code generation and never enter the module graph at all, so the
structural edge had to stand in for all of them. The consequence is that no per-name
usage could reach a locals module *by construction*, for every faceted module, whether
or not mangling was involved. Those per-export references are now real graph edges, and
the structural one is demoted to `ExportUsage::evaluation()` — which is all it was ever
for (side effects and evaluation order).

**Usage has to propagate, not just be present.** The synthesized per-export edges
declare `ImportUsage::Exports({name})`, so an edge is live exactly when the facade
export it implements is live. Declaring `TopLevel` would carry the names but pin every
local export alive — the opposite of the intent.

**`EcmascriptModulePartReference::code_generation` didn't honor
`chunking_context.unused_references()`**, unlike `EsmAssetReference::code_generation`
which has always checked it. The `all()` edge hid this, because an `All` edge is never
pruned. Once the structural edge became a prunable `Evaluation` edge, a side-effect-free
locals module could be dropped from the chunk while codegen still emitted its import —
`module factory is not available` at runtime. The part reference now agrees with the
graph, the same way a normal import does. This is a pre-existing inconsistency that only
became reachable here.

The result is webpack's output — mangled internals, original names on the surface:

```js
locals:  .s(["Q",0,"a-value","A",0,"b-value","U",0,"default-value", …])
facade:  .s(["ENUM_A",()=>e.Q,"ENUM_B",()=>e.A,"default",()=>e.U, …])
```

### Testing

Every affected fixture previously asserted the back-off, so the assertions move with the
behavior — but every *value* and `Object.keys` assertion in them is untouched and still
passes, which is what demonstrates the materialized namespace is faithful:

- `mangle-materialized-namespace` graduates out of `__skipped__` (that directory is now
  empty and removed). It was the tripwire for exactly this feature.
- `mangle-destructuring`, `mangle-magic-comments`, `mangle-many-exports` and
  `mangle-cjs-consumer` now expect their modules to be mangled. The CommonJS one is the
  interesting case: a `require()` consumer still reads correct values *and*
  `Object.keys()` still contains the original names, while the module underneath is
  mangled.
- `side-effects-unsorted-modules` now trims a side-effect-free module Turbopack couldn't
  trim before, matching webpack. Its `TODO` about being unable to follow namespace
  re-exports while tree shaking is resolved and removed.

Suite: 545 unit + 272 execution + 125 snapshot, all green, `fmt` and `clippy` clean.

Because these paths are what a real build exercises and the fixtures alone did not catch
the codegen/graph disagreement, this was also verified end to end: the five app-dir e2e
suites that an earlier revision of this change broke all pass under CI's
`__NEXT_CACHE_COMPONENTS=true` (`dynamic-import`, `client-module-with-package-type`,
`actions-streaming`, `global-not-found`, `concurrent-router-queue`), and a production
`next build` with mangling enabled compiles and prerenders.

issue.title: [Moonshot] Align thinking and reasoning options with model schemas
issue.body:
## Endpoint and priority

`POST /v1/chat/completions` — **P0** because current options can produce schema-invalid model requests.

## Official specification evidence

The [OpenAPI document](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) defines `reasoning_effort` only for K3 (`low|high|max`), K2.7 thinking as always `enabled`/`all`, K2.6 thinking as `enabled|disabled` with optional `keep: all|null`, K2.5 thinking without `keep`, and no `budget_tokens`. The [thinking guide](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-thinking-models) confirms these model-specific rules.

## Current behavior

The provider can send `reasoning_effort` to any model, `thinking` to K3/V1, `disabled` to K2.7, non-standard `budget_tokens`, and `{keep:"all"}` without the schema-required `type`.

## Expected behavior

Produce only model-valid thinking/reasoning fields, preserve compatible deprecated inputs with warnings where safe, and warn/omit impossible settings.

## Proposed implementation

Centralize model capability classification, make `budgetTokens` a deprecated runtime compatibility input that is omitted, gate generic/explicit reasoning effort to K3, normalize K2.7/K2.6/K2.5 thinking shapes, and validate preserved-thinking support.

## Acceptance criteria

- Request bodies match each official model schema.
- K2.7 cannot emit disabled thinking; K3/V1 cannot emit `thinking`.
- `budget_tokens` is never sent.
- Explicit and generic options have deterministic precedence and actionable warnings.
- Public provider option types/docs describe supported values.

## Required artifacts

Comprehensive unit matrix, provider-option type tests, documentation and examples, patch changeset; fixtures only if response behavior changes.

## Backport applicability

- v6: expected applicable with LanguageModelV3 warning/type adaptation.
- v5: expected partially applicable only where its provider/openai-compatible option surface can represent the controls; do not replace the release's core provider architecture solely to force the backport.

issue.body:
## Audit scope

Audit `@ai-sdk/moonshotai` against Moonshot's latest official API specification and first-party guides. This issue tracks one independently shippable sub-issue per gap, primary implementation PRs, and v6/v5 backports.

### Official sources

- [Moonshot OpenAPI document](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) — OpenAPI `3.1.0`, document version `1.0.0`; retrieved 2026-08-25; server `https://api.moonshot.ai`; SHA-256 `d22bc0c254c5cdb23166c4fa866931ade8cfe5c0d465e7f930361529417e4760`.
- [Chat Completions reference](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/chat) — first-party rendered endpoint reference.
- [Model parameters](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/models-overview), [model catalog](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/models), [thinking](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-thinking-models), [structured output](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/response_format), [Partial Mode](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/partial), [dynamic tools](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-dynamic-tool-loading), [vision](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-vision-model), and [errors](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/errors) — first-party supplemental evidence retrieved 2026-08-25.

### Production endpoints currently used

The provider calls only `POST https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/chat/completions` (or the configured `baseURL` plus `/chat/completions`). It sends `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, `Content-Type: application/json`, the AI SDK user-agent suffix, configured headers, and per-call headers. There are no path or query parameters. Non-streaming requests expect JSON `ChatCompletionResponse`; streaming requests add `stream: true` and `stream_options.include_usage: true`, parse SSE `ChatCompletionChunk` events, and stop at `[DONE]`. Errors use the official JSON error envelope. The provider performs no polling, upload, or download calls; `ms://` values are references created by Moonshot's Files API but are only passed through this endpoint.

### Gap analysis — `POST /v1/chat/completions`

#### P0 — incorrect requests or broken parsing

- Gate sampling fields by model. Kimi K3/K2.7/K2.6/K2.5 reject explicit sampling controls, while Moonshot V1 accepts bounded values; the provider currently sends generic sampling fields to every model.
- Align thinking/reasoning fields by model. The provider can send unsupported `reasoning_effort`, unsupported `thinking`, non-schema `budget_tokens`, K2.7 `disabled`, or `thinking.keep` without the schema-required `type`.
- Gate `tool_choice: "required"`. Official model guidance limits required tool choice; the provider forwards it to models that reject it.
- Normalize and explicitly mark structured-output schemas strict. Current response schemas receive only an ad hoc `$schema` removal and omit the documented `strict` control, causing MFJS schema rejection or non-strict behavior.
- Validate image/video MIME types. The converter currently sends any `image/*` or `video/*`, including formats the official API rejects.
- Accept documented streaming variants. The schema requires a tool-call `index` that the official chunk schema omits and ignores choice-level usage, so valid streams can fail or lose usage.

#### P1 — documented commonly used functionality missing

- Enable native JSON-schema structured output for Moonshot V1, which is covered by the shared official response-format schema but currently downgraded to JSON object mode.
- Support native `ms://` provider file references and text file parts; the provider advertises native references but the converter rejects them.
- Support `logprobs` and `top_logprobs`, including non-streaming and streaming metadata.
- Support participant `name` on system, user, and assistant messages.
- Support Partial Mode via `partial: true` on the final assistant message.
- Support Kimi K3 dynamic tool-loading system messages.

#### P2 — optional fields, metadata, and validation

- Support predicted outputs through the documented `prediction` request field.
- Send preferred `max_completion_tokens` instead of deprecated `max_tokens`.
- Preserve response object, choice index, message role, and tool-call type metadata instead of dropping them.
- Preserve official error `type` and `code` data, including streamed error events.

#### P3 — docs, examples, and model alignment

- Add the official Moonshot V1 auto/vision model IDs and align docs/examples with current K3/K2.7 guidance and deprecations.

### Documented specification gaps and contradictions

- The request documents `logprobs`, but response/chunk schemas omit its exact shape. The official overview states OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility and recommends the official OpenAI SDK; OpenAI-compatible shapes are secondary evidence for this field.
- The generic request `Message` schema omits assistant `reasoning_content`/`tool_calls` and tool `tool_call_id`, while Moonshot's official thinking and tool guides require them. Existing working support is retained.
- Usage appears both at chunk top level and as an optional choice field. The guide examples use top-level usage; the implementation should accept both without double-counting.
- Streaming tool-call examples use `index`, but the published `ChoiceDelta` tool-call schema omits it. The parser should accept both.
- The shared content schema permits video broadly, while the vision guide names K3/K2.6/K2.7 and excludes K2.5. Existing K2.5 support was live-verified in the provider history; no restrictive model gate is proposed without unambiguous first-party evidence.
- The schema default for JSON-schema `strict` is true, while the structured-output guide warns K2.6 may be non-strict when omitted and recommends sending it explicitly.
- `max_tokens` is deprecated in OpenAPI, but some first-party examples still use it.
- `n` is limited to Moonshot V1, but the AI SDK language-model contract represents one selected generation. Adding it would silently drop choices or require core architecture expansion, so it is intentionally not implemented.

## Audit scope

Audit `@ai-sdk/moonshotai` against Moonshot's latest official API specification and first-party guides. This issue tracks one independently shippable sub-issue per gap, primary implementation PRs, and v6/v5 backports.

### Official sources

- [Moonshot OpenAPI document](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) — OpenAPI `3.1.0`, document version `1.0.0`; retrieved 2026-08-25; server `https://api.moonshot.ai`; SHA-256 `d22bc0c254c5cdb23166c4fa866931ade8cfe5c0d465e7f930361529417e4760`.
- [Chat Completions reference](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/chat) — first-party rendered endpoint reference.
- [Model parameters](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/models-overview), [model catalog](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/models), [thinking](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-thinking-models), [structured output](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/response_format), [Partial Mode](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/partial), [dynamic tools](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-dynamic-tool-loading), [vision](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-vision-model), and [errors](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/errors) — first-party supplemental evidence retrieved 2026-08-25.

### Production endpoints currently used

The provider calls only `POST https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/chat/completions` (or the configured `baseURL` plus `/chat/completions`). It sends `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, `Content-Type: application/json`, the AI SDK user-agent suffix, configured headers, and per-call headers. There are no path or query parameters. Non-streaming requests expect JSON `ChatCompletionResponse`; streaming requests add `stream: true` and `stream_options.include_usage: true`, parse SSE `ChatCompletionChunk` events, and stop at `[DONE]`. Errors use the official JSON error envelope. The provider performs no polling, upload, or download calls; `ms://` values are references created by Moonshot's Files API but are only passed through this endpoint.

### Gap analysis — `POST /v1/chat/completions`

#### P0 — incorrect requests or broken parsing

- Gate sampling fields by model. Kimi K3/K2.7/K2.6/K2.5 reject explicit sampling controls, while Moonshot V1 accepts bounded values; the provider currently sends generic sampling fields to every model.
- Align thinking/reasoning fields by model. The provider can send unsupported `reasoning_effort`, unsupported `thinking`, non-schema `budget_tokens`, K2.7 `disabled`, or `thinking.keep` without the schema-required `type`.
- Gate `tool_choice: "required"`. Official model guidance limits required tool choice; the provider forwards it to models that reject it.
- Normalize and explicitly mark structured-output schemas strict. Current response schemas receive only an ad hoc `$schema` removal and omit the documented `strict` control, causing MFJS schema rejection or non-strict behavior.
- Validate image/video MIME types. The converter currently sends any `image/*` or `video/*`, including formats the official API rejects.
- Accept documented streaming variants. The schema requires a tool-call `index` that the official chunk schema omits and ignores choice-level usage, so valid streams can fail or lose usage.

#### P1 — documented commonly used functionality missing

- Enable native JSON-schema structured output for Moonshot V1, which is covered by the shared official response-format schema but currently downgraded to JSON object mode.
- Support native `ms://` provider file references and text file parts; the provider advertises native references but the converter rejects them.
- Support `logprobs` and `top_logprobs`, including non-streaming and streaming metadata.
- Support participant `name` on system, user, and assistant messages.
- Support Partial Mode via `partial: true` on the final assistant message.
- Support Kimi K3 dynamic tool-loading system messages.

#### P2 — optional fields, metadata, and validation

- Support predicted outputs through the documented `prediction` request field.
- Send preferred `max_completion_tokens` instead of deprecated `max_tokens`.
- Preserve response object, choice index, message role, and tool-call type metadata instead of dropping them.
- Preserve official error `type` and `code` data, including streamed error events.

#### P3 — docs, examples, and model alignment

- Add the official Moonshot V1 auto/vision model IDs and align docs/examples with current K3/K2.7 guidance and deprecations.

### Documented specification gaps and contradictions

- The request documents `logprobs`, but response/chunk schemas omit its exact shape. The official overview states OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility and recommends the official OpenAI SDK; OpenAI-compatible shapes are secondary evidence for this field.
- The generic request `Message` schema omits assistant `reasoning_content`/`tool_calls` and tool `tool_call_id`, while Moonshot's official thinking and tool guides require them. Existing working support is retained.
- Usage appears both at chunk top level and as an optional choice field. The guide examples use top-level usage; the implementation should accept both without double-counting.
- Streaming tool-call examples use `index`, but the published `ChoiceDelta` tool-call schema omits it. The parser should accept both.
- The shared content schema permits video broadly, while the vision guide names K3/K2.6/K2.7 and excludes K2.5. Existing K2.5 support was live-verified in the provider history; no restrictive model gate is proposed without unambiguous first-party evidence.
- The schema default for JSON-schema `strict` is true, while the structured-output guide warns K2.6 may be non-strict when omitted and recommends sending it explicitly.
- `max_tokens` is deprecated in OpenAPI, but some first-party examples still use it.
- `n` is limited to Moonshot V1, but the AI SDK language-model contract represents one selected generation. Adding it would silently drop choices or require core architecture expansion, so it is intentionally not implemented.

## Endpoint and priority

`POST /v1/chat/completions` — **P1** because the documented token-probability feature is unavailable and response data would be dropped.

## Official specification evidence

The [OpenAPI document](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) defines request `logprobs` and `top_logprobs` (`0..20`, requiring logprobs). It does not define the exact response shape; the [official API overview](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/overview) states OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility and recommends the official OpenAI SDK, whose Chat Completions logprob types are the secondary source.

## Current behavior

No provider options exist, no fields are sent, and response schemas/stream conversion discard log probabilities.

## Expected behavior

Expose validated provider options, automatically enable logprobs for `topLogprobs`, and preserve non-streaming/streaming logprob data in provider metadata.

## Proposed implementation

Mirror established AI SDK OpenAI-compatible logprob schemas and metadata mapping while clearly documenting the secondary-evidence dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- Valid request fields are serialized and invalid `topLogprobs` values fail option parsing.
- `topLogprobs` implies `logprobs: true`.
- Generate and stream results expose stable metadata without affecting text output.
- Null/omitted variants parse.

## Required artifacts

Unit, stream, fixture, and provider-option type tests; docs/example; patch changeset.

## Backport applicability

Expected applicable to v6. v5 applicability depends on its LanguageModelV2 metadata and OpenAI-compatible response hooks; document exact missing types/hooks if not applicable.

`KimiK3DynamicToolMessage` in the [OpenAPI document](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) is a system message with `tools` and no `content`. ## Acceptance criteria

- K3 emits `{role:"system",tools:[...]}` without content.
- Tool schemas are normalized consistently.
- Non-K3 official models do not receive dynamic messages and get actionable diagnostics.
- Ordinary system messages remain unchanged.

## Required artifacts

Converter/model/tool unit tests, type tests, docs/example, patch changeset; no response fixture required.

## Backport applicability

Expected applicable to v6 only if its prompt/message option contracts can represent the alternate system message. v5 is likely not applicable without provider-owned conversion.

issue.body:
## Endpoint and priority

`POST /v1/chat/completions` — **P1** because Moonshot's documented Partial Mode cannot be requested.

## Official specification evidence

The [OpenAPI `Message` schema](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/openapi.json) defines `partial:boolean` default false. The [Partial Mode guide](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/partial) requires `partial:true` on the final assistant message and documents response-format interaction.

## Current behavior

Assistant message conversion has no `partial` option or placement validation.

## Expected behavior

Expose a typed assistant-message option, serialize it only on the final assistant message, and reject/warn on invalid placement or incompatible structured-output usage according to established provider conventions.

## Proposed implementation

Extend assistant message provider options, pass conversation position/response format into conversion, and enforce official constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- A final assistant prefix sends `partial:true`.
- Invalid placement is caught before the API call.
- Documented response-format interaction produces clear behavior.
- Other assistant messages are unchanged.

## Required artifacts

Converter/model unit tests, type tests, docs/example, patch changeset; no response fixture required.

## Backport applicability

Expected applicable to v6 if message provider options are available. v5 likely lacks a provider-specific converter hook and may be not applicable.

### Feature Analysis

**Feature is not available.**

### Feature Description

- Allow users to mark the final Moonshot assistant message as a partial response prefix, serialize `partial: true`, reject invalid placement before the request, and clearly handle its interaction with structured output.
- The current Moonshot converter ignores message-level provider options, `MoonshotAIAssistantMessage` has no `partial` field, exported Moonshot options only cover request-level settings, and the focused converter probe emitted an unchanged assistant message without `partial`.

### AI SDK Fit

- This fits the provider adapter architecture because Partial Mode is Moonshot-specific and can use existing message-level `providerOptions` without introducing a cross-provider abstraction or changing `@ai-sdk/provider`.
- DeepSeek assistant prefix completion provides a close repository precedent with a typed assistant-message option, provider-side parsing, final-message validation, serialization, tests, and provider documentation.
- Serialization, placement validation, and response-format handling are dimensions of one prefix-completion contract rather than independently valuable features, so the request should not be split.

### Implications / Considerations

- The main implementation should remain limited to `@ai-sdk/moonshotai`: add and export a restrictive assistant-message provider-options schema such as `MoonshotAIAssistantMessageProviderOptions` with `partial?: true`, add `partial?: true` to the private Moonshot assistant wire type, and parse message-level options during conversion.
- The converter must track message position, reject `partial: true` on non-assistant or non-final messages with an established prompt-validation error, serialize it only for the valid final assistant message, and leave all other assistant messages unchanged; following the DeepSeek pattern will likely make conversion asynchronous.
- Structured-output validation requires access to the resolved `response_format`, so `getArgs` must reorder or coordinate message conversion and response-format construction and return a warning or preflight error according to the chosen convention.
- Moonshot explicitly warns against combining Partial Mode with `response_format: { type: 'json_object' }`, while its documentation does not clearly establish whether `json_schema` is also incompatible; this distinction matters because the current provider uses `json_schema` for supported Kimi models and falls back to `json_object` otherwise.
- No public API change is required in the `ai` package or provider specification because `ModelMessage` and `LanguageModelV4Prompt` already carry message-level provider options; the new Moonshot type export would be additive and backward compatible.
- AI SDK UI message types and framework integrations need no change, but `UIMessage` does not preserve provider options, so UI applications must convert to model messages and apply the Moonshot option server-side.
- Coverage should include converter and generate/stream request-body tests, type tests for `partial: true` and rejection of `false`, invalid-role and invalid-position tests, response-format behavior, unchanged ordinary assistant messages, a Moonshot provider example and documentation section, and a patch changeset; no response fixture is necessary.
- Moonshot states that the returned completion excludes the supplied prefix, so documentation and examples must explain that applications concatenate the prefix themselves; otherwise users may omit or duplicate content.
- The feature introduces no new credential, URL-fetching, or transport surface, although the prefix remains prompt data subject to the SDK's existing logging, telemetry, and sensitive-data considerations.
- A v6 backport appears structurally straightforward because its provider prompt and Moonshot converter already receive message-level provider options; v5 also carries message provider options but delegates Moonshot conversion to the generic OpenAI-compatible model, making a v5 backport substantially more invasive rather than categorically impossible.
